digest.component_or_area: LLM runtime and provider abstraction layer
propositions: rebar's LLM runtime is designed as provider-agnostic but hardcoded for Anthropic through provider-name prefix matching across multiple modules, causing documentation to diverge from implementation
AWS Bedrock-hosted Claude is not supported despite being the primary production path, while base_url/api_key configuration is documented but rejected at runtime by _pai_check_config

Bedrock accessed via OpenAI-compatible gateway loses native capabilities: prompt caching, retrying transport, per-request timeout, native structured output, and accurate model identification in signed verdicts

The first-class tier (native builders, full fidelity) is claimed for both Anthropic and Bedrock but Bedrock lacks retry/timeout configuration: llm_retry_max_attempts and timeout_s do not reach boto3/botocore clients

A signed verdict's model field must carry structured provenance (provider, tier, endpoint, capabilities) so consumers can distinguish first-class from best-effort verdicts and detect silent capability loss

The provider-selection seam must be unified through a single factory and ModelProfile capability lookups instead of scattered provider-name prefix matching, moving all Provider construction into providers.py registry
